intro: “I need a practical wardrobe” is a starting point, not a specification. Turn it into a brief that identifies the user, contents, constraints and evidence needed to accept the design.
goals: Ask about use before choosing a form.
Write an acceptance criterion you can actually check.

sections.title: Start with the user and activity
sections.text: Identify who will use the furniture, what they will do and how often. Ask for an inventory and the dimensions of the largest item before proposing shelves. Shared use can involve different reach needs. Rank requests as essential, important or optional, and record who confirmed each requirement.
sections.caption: User → activity → contents → requirements

sections.title: Record constraints and assumptions
sections.text: Record the available space, openings, services, budget, deadline and maintenance needs. Distinguish the client’s statements from measured facts. An unknown appliance size or fixing substrate remains an open item with an owner and a design impact. Using an assumed value in a drawing does not confirm it.
sections.caption: Each assumption needs a question, an owner and an impact

sections.title: Make acceptance testable
sections.text: Connect each requirement to evidence. To store a particular bag, confirm its dimensions and test its insertion path in a drawing or mock-up. For maintenance access, identify the service point and how it can be reached. Review the brief with the client before developing options, and retain unresolved items rather than concealing them.
sections.caption: Requirement + verification evidence = acceptance criterion

example.title: From vague request to a usable brief
example.text: A client needs entrance storage for two daily bags and keys. The available space and door swing are unconfirmed. Record the inventory, measure the bags and survey the entrance. Treat the preferred colour as a choice to review with a sample.
example.decision: Decision: keep the depth and frontage open until the door swing and bag insertion paths have been checked.

quiz.question: How should an unconfirmed door swing be recorded?
options: An open assumption with an owner
quiz.explanation: The swing may change the cabinet’s position or depth, so it needs confirmation before design approval.

quiz.question: Which acceptance criterion is testable?
options: The confirmed bag can be inserted and removed without a clash
quiz.explanation: It names a known item and a movement that can be tested.

assignment.prompt: Write an entrance-storage brief for a real user. Keep unconfirmed dimensions open until the site is surveyed.
fields: Two acceptance criteria and their evidence
criteria: Each acceptance criterion has a verification method.

faq.question: Should I start with colour?
faq.answer: Record the preference, but establish use and constraints first. Review colour with a finishing sample.

title: Turn a client request into a design brief
